summary: The chunky silhouettes and distinct early-age materials are promising, and the sixth row correctly avoids a neon future. However, story colours identify the wrong sides, the Stone Age tower reads as fantasy construction, and the Wasteland needs recognisable ruined-modern ancestry rather than a uniformly brown replacement town.
problems: Rebuild the Stone Age lodging tower around a natural rock formation; its repeated engineered storeys and extensive scaffolding undermine the prehistoric setting.

Give the caravan leaders a persistent Wren-side identity using story red, not gold; make their occupational silhouettes distinguish mammoth herding, river trade, travelling court, railway, tourism and scrap convoy.
Remove the King's dominant red cloak and the unrelated modern car's red body; reserve red for Wren's side and gold for the head's side.
Transform the existing modern home, café and tower into damaged, repaired versions on matching footprints instead of replacing their architectural identities.
Separate Wasteland people, buildings and ground by value: their olive-brown silhouettes currently merge, especially in greyscale.
Reduce competing main colour families, particularly on the Bronze Age trader and medieval King; use no more than four per piece.

Present age strips and matched-scale asset views for phone review; the full board's captions and small identity details disappear at 390 px, and independently fitted thumbnails cannot establish scale against a 1.8 m person.

Supply a town-context view before approving environmental fidelity: this board does not establish Stone Age mud roads, stick-and-mud signs, wild trees or the central bonfire, nor medieval cobblestone lanes without modern sidewalks.
Repeated stacked accommodation levels and elaborate timber access read as a fantasy tower rather than unmistakably Stone Age shelter.
Small rails, ladders and platforms become visual noise at phone size.
elements.fix: Use one irregular natural crag with three broad inhabited ledges, hide windbreaks and a few thick lashed-log access elements; retain the lodging purpose and lot footprint.

problems: The medieval gold-and-blue master and modern golden-jacket guide use the head's colour language.
There is no clear persistent Wren-side identifier across the six leaders.
The medieval figure reads more as a luggage-carrying merchant than part of a travelling court.
elements.fix: Carry one broad #B3262E sash or mantle and a recognisable silhouette through all six versions, removing dominant gold. Give the medieval leader a bold minstrel or court-traveller prop, and simplify each costume to four main colour families.

problems: The shack loses the modern home's recognisable upper-storey, porch and window structure.
Clean roof patches and uniformly brown walls suggest a new timber building more than a repaired modern ruin.
Walls, base and props have weak greyscale separation.
elements.fix: Retain the modern home's foundation, porch position and surviving wall sections; expose a broken upper floor, patch it with mismatched corrugated sheets and keep pale weathered plaster against dark openings and calm dusty ground.

problems: The pitched-roof cantina does not visibly descend from the modern flat-roof espresso shop.
The tidy benches and broad clean panels lack convincing salvage construction.
The serving opening is lost in the brown mass.
elements.fix: Keep the modern café's footprint, counter frontage and damaged flat-roof frame; reuse its awning as a torn shade, add a conspicuous fire barrel and make the serving opening a single dark shape beneath pale scrap panels.

problems: The regular brown stack reads as purpose-built scaffolding rather than the modern tower after collapse.
Repeated intact floors and evenly distributed openings make the damage too orderly.
Dark framing and infill merge at small scale.
elements.fix: Preserve the modern tower's stepped structural silhouette and foundation, strip selected façade bays irregularly, retain a few dull glass panels and add two large asymmetrical repair zones with clearly lighter infill.

problems: The dominant red cloak assigns Wren's visual identity to her opponent.
Red, blue, cream, gold and dark trim compete rather than producing one clear allegiance read.
elements.fix: Replace the red cloak with #FFC633, keep a dark blue tunic and cream trim, and simplify accessories so the crown and broad gold mantle dominate at phone size.

problems: Residents, Overseer and convoy boss share similar olive-brown clothing, headwear and compact silhouettes.
The Overseer's authority and the convoy leader's opposing allegiance depend on details too small to read.
Clothing values sit too close to the dusty bases.
elements.fix: Give residents pale patched workwear, the Overseer a broad weathered gold office marker and the convoy leader a broad story-red mantle; distinguish them further with a large tool, oversized key ring and salvaged pennant respectively.

problems: The large red body creates an unassigned Wren-side colour signal.
Its saturated finish attracts more attention than the nearby people.
elements.fix: Repaint the body muted slate blue or desaturated teal, retaining dark windows and tyres with pale lamps; reserve red bodywork for an explicitly Wren-owned vehicle.
